full_judgment: 9. Admittedly, two separate khatians under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been prepared in respect of the land of the original jama i.e. C.S. Khatian No. 803. The Courts below have observed that these two khatians are the modified record-of-right Nothing transpires either from the evidence 91 the parties or from the judgments of the Courts below that those khatians have been-finally published and accepted under the provisions of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as final. There are two provisions under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act regarding preparation of the record-of-rights. Under section 19 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in view of the notification of the Government under section 17 of the Act a draft record-of-right was prepared for the purpose of acquisition of the rent-receiving interest or under the same provisions the record of right that was prepared under Chapter X of the Bengal Tenancy Act would have been revised in respect of any district, part of a district or of any local area as the Government would deem fit and necessary; The particulars which are required to be incorporated under those draft record-of-rights have been mentioned in the rules framed for the purpose. A judicial notice can be taken that the draft or the revised khatians that were directed to be prepared under section 19 of the Act was not finally published since before coming into force of Part V or the Act, which came into operation in the Noakhali district on 1.8.63. After coming into force of whole of the Part V a radical change in the scheme of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was brought in, whereby in view of sub-section (8) of section 82 the words 'raiyati' or 'tenant' as well as 'rent' were to be deemed to have been substituted by the words 'milk' an 'land revenue'. Chapter V of the Act also brought in the incident of tenancy including the right of occupancy as well as devolution of interest by way of inheritance. In view of sections . 83 and 84 of the Act. Thus question of status of the malik as well as the co-sharer malik, as are to be read in section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in view of the, provisions of section- 82 (8) of the Act, gave a new dimension in the rights and liabilities including the right to pre-empt by a co-sharer malik in respect of the transfer of any holding or portion thereof by a ma to any stranger. Section 96 has also brought a new right of pre-emption for the owners of the contiguous lands. Under section 19 provisions have been made only to prepare a draft record-of-right or to revise the re-cord-of-right prepared and finally published under Chapter X of the Bengal Tenancy Act. After coming into force of Part-V and giving the raiyats of different natures to a single status of malik, the right to hold or occupy such land for agricultural or horticultural purposes on payment of revenue direct to the Government. The word 'tenant' as has been defined under section 2(27) of the Act lost is connotation as was initially defined. It is evident that in Part—V provision has been made under section 117 of the Act for amalgamation, consolidation or subdivision of holdings. In .case of amalgamation or consolidation of holdings under section 117 (1) (a), (b) the revenue officer either of his own motion or upon any application made to him in that behalf is entitled to amalgamate or consolidate the holdings. But so far the sub-division of holdings is concerned under section 117(1) (c) of the Act it has been made imperative that the sub-division of joint tenancy for distribution of rent thereof can be made by the revenue officer only upon an application made to him by one or more co-sharer tenants and no order for such sub-division shall be passed unless reasonable notice is given to the parties concerned to appear and to be heard by him in the matter. It has further been provided under sub-section (3) of section 117 that that when an order under sub section (1) has been passed sub-dividing a joint holding, such sub-division may be demarcated on the ground and shown on the cadastral survey map. Thus the scheme of sub-division is very much clear for the purpose of adjudication that has been provided under Chapter XII of Part-V of the Act.
